URL: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c794xw7p2dqo
TITLE: HS2 could cost up to £102.7bn and trains will be slower than first planned
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-19 12:44 (updated 14:34)
AUTHORS: Katy Austin (Transport correspondent), Rachel Clun (Business reporter)
SOURCE: BBC

KEY:
- New cost range: £87.7bn-£102.7bn in 2025 prices
- Roughly DOUBLE the price range under previous Conservative government (when readjusted to 2019 prices)
- Trains won't start until 2036-2039 (vs most recent target of 2033) — up to 6 years late
- Top speed reduced from 360km/h (224mph) to 320km/h to save up to £2.5bn + accelerate delivery by 1 year
- £44.2bn already spent as of March 2026
- 2 of 3 cost increase due to: underestimate by previous government, inefficient delivery, missed scope; 1/3 due to inflation
- HS2 Ltd CEO Mark Wild target: 2037 at £92.2bn
- Full service Euston-Curzon St + West Coast Main Line connection: 2040-2043

HEIDI ALEXANDER (Transport Secretary, Labour) QUOTES:
- Labour inherited "litany of failure"
- "Instead of signalling the country's ambition, HS2 became a signal of the country's decline"
- "If it seems like an obscene increase in time and costs, it is because it is"
- "If it seems like I'm angry, it is because I am"
- "I can confirm today that it could cost almost as much to cancel the line as it would to finish it, while delivering none of the benefits"
- "This country can build big things, we just need competent people at the helm to deliver them"
- Project committed to delivering despite cost increases

REACTIONS:
- Shadow transport minister Jerome Mayhew accepted early years had "delay and cost overruns"; HS2 Ltd "failing to maintain control of the budget"; Dept for Transport "allowing them to get away with it"
- Demanded "consequential legislative changes" to stop future overruns
- Andy Meaney (contributed to Oakervee HS2 review): "continual failure of decision making right back to the conception of the scheme 16, 17 years ago"; speed reduction "should have been taken a long time ago"

HISTORY TIMELINE:
- 2012 Jan: original plan London-Birmingham + Leeds + Manchester legs, opening 2026
- 2013 Jun: budget £42.6bn (2011 prices, Osborne)
- 2015 Nov: £55.7bn (2015 prices)
- 2021 Nov: Eastern leg to Leeds cancelled
- 2023 Oct: Sunak scraps western leg to Manchester
- 2024 Jan: HS2 Ltd boss says could be £65bn+
- 2026 May: now £88-£103bn
